observacoes: Jargao regulatorio/contabil abstrato — claims mantidas o mais literais possivel ao texto original para reduzir risco de interpretacao subjetiva. Fornecedores/beneficiarios e pagadores de valores devidos NAO sao stakeholders (nao logam no sistema, sao partes externas afetadas pelas transacoes). Conteudo em ingles porque o cenario-fonte e em ingles (mesma convencao dos gabaritos RAGAS existentes).

em_escopo: General ledger as the central component of the system
Classifying and tracking transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center
Funds control (preventing obligation/spending above the appropriated amount)
Processing payments to vendors/payees, with confirmation of destination
Recording and following up on amounts owed to the agency, including chasing missed payments
Cost management (what each program costs and produces)
Producing formal financial statements and reports for management, oversight bodies, and eventual public release
A real audit trail and security controls over who can access what
Web access, not restricted to a single terminal
Integration with other existing agency systems
fora_de_escopo: Optional ('nice to have') features not required by law or regulation — deprioritized in the first round in favor of mandatory requirements
premissas: PA-01: [INFERRED] The agency already has other existing systems that the financial system needs to integrate with.
PA-02: The system needs to be in substantial compliance with FFMIA before any eventual formal audit.
restricoes: REST-01 (Regulatory): The system must be in substantial compliance with FFMIA (Federal Financial Management Improvement Act) requirements.
REST-02 (Prioritization): Optional features not required by law or regulation are left out of the first round of development.
REST-03 (Usability): The system must be operable by non-technical finance staff, not only by IT staff.

stakeholders.descricao: Financial systems analyst — day-to-day user of the system.
Accountant — day-to-day user, responsible for accounting records.
Program manager — consults cost and performance data of programs for budget decisions.
Agency operations staff — needs to pull numbers from the system to run the agency.
Auditor — periodically reviews the system to verify compliance and control.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The system must never allow obligating or spending more than what was actually appropriated (funds control) — a hard, non-negotiable rule.
The general ledger is the central component of the system; every other function depends on it.
Optional features not required by law or regulation are deprioritized relative to mandatory requirements in the first round.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must maintain a general ledger as its central component, on which the other functions depend.
The system must classify and track transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
The system must prevent an obligation or expenditure from exceeding the amount actually appropriated (funds control).
The system must process payments to vendors/payees.
The system must track and confirm that a payment reached the correct destination.
The system must record amounts owed to the agency (receivables).
The system must support following up on/collecting receivables when payment is not made.
The system must support cost management, measuring what each program costs and what it produces.
The system must produce formal financial statements and reports for agency management.
The system must produce formal financial statements and reports for oversight bodies.
The system must support the eventual public release of financial statements and reports.
The system must maintain a real audit trail of who accessed or changed what.
The system must enforce security controls over who can access what.
The system must provide web access to users, instead of restricting them to a single terminal.
The system must integrate with other systems already existing at the agency, instead of operating in isolation.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must handle its operational workload without performance failure.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a financial systems analyst, I want to classify and track transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center, so that program and budget managers can analyze the data.
As an accountant, I want the system to prevent obligations or spending beyond the appropriated amount, so that the agency stays within its funding limits.
As an accounts-payable owner, I want to process payments to vendors/payees and confirm they reached the correct destination, so that disbursements are accurate and traceable.
As an accounts-receivable owner, I want to record amounts owed to the agency and chase overdue payments, so that outstanding amounts are collected.
As a program manager, I want to see cost management data (what a program costs and produces), so that I can support budget decisions.
As agency management, I want formal financial statements and reports, so that I can report to oversight bodies and, eventually, the public.
As an auditor, I want to review a real audit trail and the system's access security controls, so that I can verify compliance during periodic reviews.
As agency operations staff, I want to access the system over the web from multiple locations, so that I'm not restricted to a single terminal.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Record and classify transaction — a user records a financial transaction in the general ledger, classified by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
Process vendor payment — the system processes a payment to a vendor/payee and confirms it reached the correct destination, respecting the funds control limit.
Track receivable — the system records an amount owed to the agency and flags it for follow-up when payment is not made.
Generate financial report — a user generates formal financial statements/reports for management, oversight bodies, or public release.
Audit system access — an auditor reviews the system's audit trail and access controls.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a transaction that would exceed the funds appropriated for its fund/program, when it is submitted, then the system prevents the obligation/expenditure from being recorded.
Given a payment issued to a vendor/payee, when the payment is processed, then the system tracks and confirms that it reached the correct destination.
Given a receivable with an overdue payment, when the due date passes without payment, then the system flags the case for follow-up.
Given a request for a formal financial statement, when it is generated, then the result is suitable for submission to management and to oversight bodies.
Given a user accessing the system, when any action is performed, then the system records it in an audit trail that identifies who did what.
